subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should managed npm plugin roots inherit OpenClaw's host workspace overrides wholesale, inherit only a maintainer-approved subset, or keep the current policy and surface an Express 4/path-to-regexp diagnostic?
rationale: The source-level failure is clear, but the right fix changes the dependency-ownership boundary for all managed npm plugin installs and can affect security pins, plugin compatibility, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Scoped managed-root override policy
options.body: Filter or scope host overrides so managed plugin roots preserve plugin-owned dependency ranges like Express 4's path-to-regexp 0.1.x while retaining explicitly approved OpenClaw security/peer pins.

options.title: Validator and diagnostic only
options.body: Keep override propagation as-is but detect Express 4/path-to-regexp conflicts during install or doctor and produce an actionable error for plugin publishers and users.

options.title: Keep plugin-owned workaround
options.body: Document that third-party Express 4 plugins must ship their own override or migrate to Express 5, accepting that OpenClaw-managed installs can still fail until publishers update.

recommendation.title: Scoped managed-root override policy
recommendation.body: Filter or scope host overrides so managed plugin roots preserve plugin-owned dependency ranges like Express 4's path-to-regexp 0.1.x while retaining explicitly approved OpenClaw security/peer pins.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc has recent direct history in managed override propagation, plugin install security, and release dependency state.
